name: Impedance Calculator
blurb: characteristic impedance of microstrip, stripline and differential pairs from the stackup
intro: Impedance of a trace from its width, copper thickness and the dielectric to its reference plane(s), and the width that hits a target. Single lines use the Hammerstad-Jensen (microstrip) and Wheeler (stripline) closed forms; pairs use the AN-905 / IPC-2141 coupling approximation.

inputs.label: Gap between pair traces S
inputs.help: Edge to edge; only used for differential pairs.

inputs.label: Dielectric height H (H1)
inputs.help: Trace to its reference plane. Stripline: to the plane below.

inputs.label: Stripline: dielectric above H2
inputs.help: Trace to the plane above; set equal to H for a centred stripline.

inputs.label: Copper thickness T
inputs.help: 0.5 oz = 17.5 µm, 1 oz = 35 µm, 2 oz = 70 µm. Outer layers gain ~20 µm of plating.

inputs.label: Dielectric constant Er
inputs.help: FR-4 about 4.2-4.6; use the fab's value for the prepreg or core.

inputs.label: Target impedance
inputs.help: Optional: the tool solves the width that gives it.

examples.title: USB 90 Ω pair on the outer layer of a 4-layer board
50 Ω stripline on an inner layer, mils

usage: Give the line type (microstrip, stripline, diff-microstrip, diff-stripline), lengths W, S, H, H2 in the unit chosen by 'units' (mm or mil), copper thickness T in µm, Er, and optionally a target impedance in ohms. Returns Z0 (and Zdiff for pairs), effective Er, delay in ps/mm, L and C per mm, the width that meets the target, and a width sweep. Use it to size controlled-impedance traces before asking the fab for their stackup; pair results are ±5-10 %.
sources: E. Hammerstad, O. Jensen, 'Accurate Models for Microstrip Computer-Aided Design', IEEE MTT-S 1980
B. C. Wadell, Transmission Line Design Handbook, Artech House 1991, sections 3.5.1 and 3.5.3 (Wheeler stripline, offset stripline)
National Semiconductor AN-905, Transmission Line RAPIDESIGNER Operation and Applications Guide (edge-coupled pairs); IPC-2141A
